messages.content: Write an announcement telling customers that a service is moving to a new platform next quarter. Around 250 words.

output:
Placeholders in brackets — swap in your specifics.

---

**Subject: [Service] moves to [new platform] in [Q1 2027]**

Hi [name],

Starting [date], [Service] will run on [new platform]. We're telling you now so you can plan around it.

Why: [current platform can't do X]. The new one gives us [concrete thing — faster restores, regional hosting, a real API].

**What changes for you**

- Your sign-in URL becomes [new URL]. The old one redirects until [date].
- API endpoints move to [new base]. The old ones keep working through [date], then return 410.
- [Feature X] behaves differently: [one sentence].

**What doesn't change**

Your data, account history, billing date, and existing integration credentials. We migrate all of it. You don't need to export or re-upload anything.

**The cutover**

[Date], [time range] [timezone]. Expect [N minutes/hours] where the service is read-only. Live status at [status page].

**What we need from you**

Nothing, unless you've hardcoded [old URL] somewhere. If you have, update it before [date]. If you're on [legacy plan] or [SDK below vX], reply to this email and we'll walk through it with you — those two cases need a manual step.

We'll send a reminder two weeks out, and again the day before. If something breaks after the move, [support channel] reaches us fastest, and we're staffing it heavier for the first two weeks.

[Name]
[Title], [Company]

---

Two things worth deciding before you send: whether to name the old platform (usually don't), and whether the read-only window is short enough to state as a number rather than a range. A range reads like you don't know.
